summary: Redwood AE/SE demoed Eval/Quality Monitoring (Console + Optimize features) to Ember Finance. Focus on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Customer interested in pilot to validate regression detection and cost/latency tradeoffs. Security and data residency questions surfaced. Next steps: send pricing and security docs, get prompt set, schedule pilot kickoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Sofia from Redwood, diego and i will run through our eval and quality monitoring demo today. can everyone hear ok?
[00:06] Ravi Patel: Yep loud and clear, thanks Sofia.
[00:11] Aisha Khan: good here.
[00:15] Diego Martinez: Great, i'll share my screen in a sec, uh okay switching to console.
[00:28] (screen share starts)
[00:31] Sofia Chen: quick agenda: show the Console eval workspace, how prompt sets are organized, setting up regression alerts, then an A/B comparison demo using Optimize and API examples. we'll keep time for Q&A and security questions at the end.
[00:46] Lena Moore: thats perfect, we're mainly interested in regression detection because our product is sensitive to hallucinations, and we need to detect quality regressions quickly.
[00:55] Diego Martinez: totally, that's a common ask. first up: prompt sets. so here on Console you can create a prompt set which is basically a named collection of prompts and expected outputs, metadata like input type, labels, and golden responses. you can upload via CSV or connect to a test bucket.
[01:13] Ravi Patel: can we tag prompts by feature and version? we run changes across multiple flows.
[01:18] Diego Martinez: yes we support tags and versioning per prompt set, and you can pin a baseline model version. so for regressions we compare current model output distributions to that pinned baseline.
[01:30] (brief pause, typing)
[01:37] Sofia Chen: quick note: transcription may show like 'key cache' instead of 'KV cache' in some places, apologies for audio labeling.
[01:44] Ravi Patel: ha noted.
[01:47] Diego Martinez: next, evaluation metrics: you can pick built in metrics like BLEU, ROUGE, exact match, and also custom validators - regex checks, JSON schema validators, or ML classifiers. we often recommend a mix for production systems.
[02:03] Lena Moore: we do a lot of structured output, json blobs returned to downstream systems, so schema validation is critical.
[02:10] Diego Martinez: right, so in the demo i have a prompt set for 'transaction-summarization' with golden json responses. i'll run a quick batch eval.
[02:20] (batch run initiated)
[02:28] Diego Martinez: you'll see the run progress, we give per-prompt diffs, token-level cost, and latency percentiles. these show up on the Console under the run results.
[02:41] Aisha Khan: latency looks like 120-150ms p50 from the run, is that real?
[02:46] Diego Martinez: depends on model and deployment, this demo uses a mid-size open model on hosted infra—so numbers are demo-only. in a Dedicated pool you'd get more consistent p50/p95.
[02:58] Sofia Chen: to speak to cost/latency tradeoffs, Optimize will suggest quantization and batching profiles for your workload, and you can run a simulated cost estimate for the run.
[03:12] Ravi Patel: can Optimize suggest alternate models for similar quality at lower cost?
[03:16] Diego Martinez: yep — it ranks model candidates by quality delta and cost delta, so you can do A/B comparisons automatically.
[03:24] (typing)
[03:30] Diego Martinez: switching to regression alerts now. you can define alert rules on any metric from your eval runs: e.g. increase in hallucination-rate +5% relative to baseline, schema validation drop below 98%, or custom classifier drift.
[03:42] Sofia Chen: alerts can be routed to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook; we also send context links to the failing prompts and a diff view.
[03:53] Lena Moore: do the alerts do windows or just point-in-time? we want to avoid noise on single flakey prompts.
[03:58] Diego Martinez: good question—alerts support rolling-window logic and thresholding; you can require N failures in M runs before firing.
[04:08] Ravi Patel: how accurate are the auto-classifiers? we may need human-in-the-loop review.
[04:13] Diego Martinez: classifiers are pluggable; Redwood ships with a set of default detectors, but you can attach your own models or human review workflows. actions can include auto-rollback of a rollout if the regression severity crosses a defined SLO.
[04:26] (short crosstalk)
[04:30] Aisha Khan: curious about A/B comparisons — how do you split traffic and collect metrics?
[04:35] Diego Martinez: two ways: controlled A/B via our routing policies, or offline A/B by running the same prompt set against two model versions and comparing metrics. online A/B supports traffic allocation, consistent user hashing, and can route by policy (latency/cost/region).
[04:50] Lena Moore: we'd probably start with offline A/B on our most important flows.
[04:55] Sofia Chen: perfect. i'll demo an offline A/B run now — running prompt set against baseline v1 and candidate v2, then show delta table.
[05:05] (run starts)
[05:18] Diego Martinez: here is the delta, you can sort by metric impact, and click into examples with side-by-side outputs. note: transcription sometimes shows 'quantize' as 'can this' in the transcript but ignore that.
[05:33] Ravi Patel: nice, i like the side-by-side diffs. can we annotate examples and push them back to training or to a curated prompt list?
[05:40] Diego Martinez: yep you can flag examples which creates a curated set; those can be exported or used in supervised fine-tuning workflows.
[05:48] Lena Moore: what about alerting on production traffic rather than scheduled eval runs?
[05:53] Diego Martinez: you can attach a live sampling hook to production traffic (we do sampling at configurable rates) and run the sampled messages through the same eval pipeline. that gives near-real-time signal.
[06:07] Aisha Khan: does sampling have material cost impact?
[06:10] Diego Martinez: small relative to full traffic if you sample at 1-5%, but cost depends on model size and sampling rate; Optimize will show cost estimate for your sampling config.
[06:22] Sofia Chen: security note — for Private/Dedicated you can keep eval data inside your VPC; logs and KV caches can be customer-managed and encrypted with your KMS.
[06:33] Ravi Patel: we have strong requirements around KMS and audit logs, any references?
[06:38] Diego Martinez: i'll share SOC2 and KMS integration docs after the call (link in follow-up). we support customer-managed keys and detailed audit logs per request.
[06:50] (typing)
[06:55] Lena Moore: timeline question — how quickly can we spin up a pilot?
[06:58] Sofia Chen: typically 2-3 weeks to stand up a pilot on Hosted with eval runs; Dedicated or Private takes longer for infra and contracts.
[07:08] Ravi Patel: budget wise, we're evaluating cost of adding this monitoring vs building in-house.
[07:13] Sofia Chen: totally — that's why Optimize's cost modeling is useful; it gives you comparative estimates and suggests batching and quantization to reduce per-token cost.
[07:24] (pause)
[07:28] Diego Martinez: i want to show a short example of a regression alert workflow — i'll induce a failing prompt and show detection.
[07:34] (demo: inject failing prompt)
[07:40] Diego Martinez: alert fired, here's the Slack notification and the Console link. it shows top failing prompts, metric deltas, and recommended actions (rollback or annotate).
[07:52] Lena Moore: is rollback automatic? we need approval steps.
[07:55] Diego Martinez: you can configure auto-rollback only with guardrails; many customers opt for manual approval with one-click rollback from Console.
[08:04] Ravi Patel: how do you handle false positives? we need rates to be low.
[08:08] Diego Martinez: false positives reduced via rolling window, classifier thresholds, and human review gating. we saw in trials false-positive rates under X for well-tuned rules, but we'll validate with your prompts in the pilot.
[08:22] Sofia Chen: quick note on integrations — APIs are straightforward. you can call Redwood eval endpoints programmatically, ingest results into your observability, or use webhooks.
[08:33] Aisha Khan: do you have SDKs? we use python and node.
[08:36] Diego Martinez: yes official SDKs for python/node/go and REST examples for bumping into CI.
[08:42] (typing)
[08:47] Lena Moore: do you keep PII in eval logs? we need redaction.
[08:52] Diego Martinez: we support automatic redaction rules at ingestion plus token-level obfuscation, and you can route eval logs to your S3 in the VPC with access controls.
[09:03] Ravi Patel: good.
[09:05] Sofia Chen: okay moving on to A/B comparison report exports — CSV, JSON, and link to the run. these include per-prompt metrics and sample outputs so you can ingest into your analytics.
[09:17] Diego Martinez: we also provide a summary metrics API for programmatic monitoring.
[09:22] (typing)
[09:28] Lena Moore: for the pilot we'll want a set of 5k prompts from our top features, and three regression scenarios.
[09:35] Ravi Patel: yes that'll help us quantify risk.
[09:38] Sofia Chen: we'll take that as an action item.
[09:41] (brief silence)
[09:46] Aisha Khan: on the deployment side, if we move to Dedicated, can we coordinate autoscaling with our internal capacity planning?
[09:54] Diego Martinez: Dedicated pools have configurable autoscaling policies and you can request reserved bursts. we provide SLOs on p50/p95 for committed capacity.
[10:06] Ravi Patel: any limitations on model types for evals — e.g., custom finetuned models?
[10:11] Diego Martinez: you can evaluate any model we host or bring your own in Private; model connectors support version pinning so your finetuned model can be the baseline.
[10:21] Sofia Chen: Q&A time — customer questions?
[10:26] Lena Moore: question on retention — how long are eval results stored?
[10:29] Diego Martinez: default 90 days for runs, longer retention as an add-on; for Private you control retention policy.
[10:37] Ravi Patel: audit trails for regressions?
[10:39] Diego Martinez: full audit trail with user actions, run ids, model versions, and who annotated examples.
[10:48] (typing)
[10:52] Aisha Khan: can we integrate failure signals into our internal ticketing?
[10:56] Sofia Chen: yes webhooks can create tickets, and we have a connector for Jira in beta.
[11:04] Ravi Patel: about data residency — our compliance team may demand EU-only hosting. is that possible?
[11:09] Diego Martinez: yes we have region-specific hosting and Private deployments in EU regions; we'll share details in the security doc.
[11:18] (screen transition)
[11:23] Diego Martinez: final demo snippet — running an A/B offline comparison with customized metric weights (we gave hallucination 2x weight for this customer). you can save a report template.
[11:38] Lena Moore: love the weighting feature.
[11:41] Sofia Chen: recap: we showed prompt sets, eval runs, regression alerts, A/B comparisons, Optimize recommendations, and deployment options.
[11:51] Ravi Patel: next steps for us: we'll prepare the prompt set and success criteria, review pilot pricing, and want SOC2 docs.
[11:59] Sofia Chen: action items noted, we'll send a follow-up email with links to the demo recording, SOC2 doc, pricing, and a pilot timeline.
[12:08] (wrap up, thanks)
[12:12] (call ends)

Note: Transcript contains occasional ASR errors and speaker attribution approximations as typical with meeting exports.
